checks: typecheck ok; targeted vitest 13 files 142 pass 0 fail (auth, invitations, admin-invitations, invite-token-leak, rate-limit.shared-store, config.env-example, config.env-secrets, security-headers, e2-second-person, family-invites-outlive-owner, lovedone.preferred-name, auth.signup-gate, continuity-security-races); full vitest NOT completed: binaries.prisma.sh blocked means no native query engine, so the client was generated locally (uncommitted) with the queryCompiler/wasm preview, under which about 27 tests in unrelated files fail identically on main (verified br2-t8+analytics: 7 fail on both), and the run was too slow on 2 CPUs (about 30/158 files in 35 min); backend-ci is the real gate; no lint script in backend; test:race not run (no concurrency change); no e2e suite exists

K1.text: Sessions are watermark-revocable: authenticate re-reads isActive and tokenVersion on every request. Refresh tokens are single-use DB rows, and replaying one revokes all sessions. Verify, reset and invite tokens are stored only as sha256 hashes and are spent by POST. Re-read on HEAD 37dffdb.

K2.text: Admin login requires a TOTP code, compared with timingSafeEqual and single-use per RFC 6238, with the secret sealed under TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY. authenticateAdmin is default-deny by role. /admin/* also needs a verified Cloudflare Access JWT, and the gate is closed when that is unset. Spot-checked.

K3.text: Full sweep: a script listed all 219 route registrations, and each one without a guard was read by hand. All private routes use authenticate, authenticateAdmin or gated. The only unguarded routes are the intentionally public /health, GET /auth/signup (returns a flag), signup/login/refresh/verify/forgot/reset, DELETE /auth/refresh (acts on the caller's own cookie), /admin/auth/login, /feedback/public-idea, invitation preview/decline (token, limited on the branch) and /billing/webhook (Stripe signature). It is an API only, so there are no 'use server' exports.

K4.text: Relies on the Opus K4 sweep of 2026-09-26 (93 routes), plus a spot check of modules added since. Check-In getRecipient/enrol call resolveMembership with assertRead/assertWrite. Notice read/unclaim scope by noticeId, recipientUserId and the escalation's lovedOneId. The five LOW oracle items from the sweep remain.

K5.text: On the branch, GET /invitations/:token/preview (30 per 10 min) and POST /invitations/:token/decline (10 per 10 min) opt into the Postgres-backed limiter that already covers every other public route. On main both were unthrottled. A test proves the 429.

K6.text: Family and admin invite tokens are stored as sha256 hashes with a 14-day expiry (inviteExpiresAt is checked on lookup) and can be revoked or renewed. The token routes send no-store, no-referrer and noindex, and the URL is masked in logs and the 404 handler. Read on HEAD, and the existing invite-token-leak test passes.

K7.text: The API sets nosniff, CSP with frame-ancestors none, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, HSTS and CORP on every response. frontend, admin-frontend and handhold-site vercel.json all set CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, nosniff and HSTS. The security-headers test passes.

K8.text: JWT_SECRET, ANALYTICS_PEPPER and TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY require 32+ characters and refuse public placeholders outside NODE_ENV=test. TOTP uses timingSafeEqual. The CF Access gate is closed when unset. Stripe signatures are verified by the SDK. git ls-files shows only .env.example. The frontends use no VITE_ variables.

K9.text: The Stripe webhook keeps the raw body in its own scope, and constructEvent checks the signature with the SDK's default 300s timestamp tolerance. Every event re-reads the subscription from Stripe, so replays converge. A throw returns non-2xx, so Stripe retries. There is no event table, but the handler is idempotent by design.

K10.text: Pino redacts auth headers, cookies and token or password fields. Request URLs and 404s mask invite tokens. buildApp refuses to boot in production without an email transport, so the log-only sender (which logs the link text) is unreachable there.

K11.text: The zod schema validates env at import, so the app does not boot on a bad value. On the branch .env.example also lists CHECKIN_CONSENT_HMAC_KEY, CHECKIN_TRANSCRIPT_KEY, FEATURE_CHECKIN and FEATURE_CHECKIN_CALLS, plus the platform and test names. A new test scans src/, scripts/ and tests/ and fails on any variable read but not listed (it fails on main with eight). FEATURE_* and RENDER_GIT_COMMIT stay outside the schema by design.

K12.text: Tests use in-process PGlite. The only path to a real Postgres is RACE_PG_URL, and harness.ts throws unless that host is localhost or 127.0.0.1 and the DB name ends in _race. That is a code-level guard (stricter than the foundation's cloud-host regex). The harness never reads DATABASE_URL. There is no e2e suite, so the production-build rule does not apply yet.

K13.text: Migrations add BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE and TRUNCATE triggers making AdminActionLog, ModerationAction and VaultAccessLog (and ProfileResolutionLog) append-only. UPDATE may only null columns, for the erasure path. A table-owning role could still drop the triggers; the production REVOKE is an OPS item.

K14.text: All three vercel.json files (handhold-site, frontend, admin-frontend) carry the foundation's ignoreCommand pattern, scoped to their own folder. PORT defaults to 4301 (Handhold's 4300-4302 row). The cron is a Render cron job running a CLI script, not an HTTP route, so the constant-time cron compare does not apply.
